subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but the durable storage model, privacy behavior, rollback/audit semantics, operator UX, and plugin API boundary are product decisions automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define Shared Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle schema/API/status/provenance semantics, then split implementation across schema, write path, and operator surfaces.

options.title: Narrow V1 To Memory Core
options.body: Implement the lifecycle only for bundled memory-core first, accepting a later compatibility alignment step for external memory plugins.

options.title: Defer Broad Lifecycle Work
options.body: Keep current search, promotion, Dreaming, and Memory Wiki behavior while concrete stale-memory symptoms remain tracked separately.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Lifecycle Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad design tracker, settle schema/API/status/provenance semantics, then split implementation across schema, write path, and operator surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema and memory-wiki history makes this the best available owner for lifecycle contract direction.
